answer: Stop at documenting that the sequencing/determination happened, carried out by whom and when, and point to the external accession record -- do not duplicate the nucleotide sequence or the tree's bootstrap-support values inside the collection database. Model the act as an E17 Type Assignment on the fish (E20 Biological Object): E17's own scope note explicitly folds molecular work in here -- 'This class also encompasses the notion of "determination," i.e. the systematic and molecular identification of a specimen in biology' -- and the SIG's background for this exact issue (Issue 77) names 'Molecular identification. e.g. via gene bank' as one of the two recognised determination methods. Record P14 carried out by (the genomics lab), P4 has time-span, P32/P33 for the technique (e.g. 'mitochondrial DNA sequencing'), and P42 assigned for whatever taxon/relationship was concluded. For the deposit itself, attach the accession number as an E42 Identifier via P1 is identified by / P48 has preferred identifier on the specimen (or on an E15 Identifier Assignment event documenting who assigned it and when), and treat the external database's own entry as an E31 Document that P70 documents the specimen -- P70 is a required property on E31's domain, i.e. any such document necessarily documents something, which is exactly the 'pointing to' relationship the curator is asking about. E42 is the right identifier class here specifically because a GenBank-style accession is used by human agents (cited, looked up), not a purely internal machine hash -- E42's own scope note carves out machine-only identifiers, not this case. This matches the CRM's own stated boundary for Natural History collections: the SIG's 1996 Monterey discussion (Issues 76/77 background) splits Natural History documentation into 'ordinary collection management' -- 'covered completely by the CIDOC CRM' -- versus more elaborate derived scientific constructs, giving ecosystem-level observations as the example of something 'beyond the practical scope of the CRM.' A phylogenetic tree with per-branch bootstrap-support values is the same shape of problem: a multi-specimen, comparative, statistically-derived dataset, not a property of this one fish, and CRM/CRMsci has no class for a tree or a bootstrap statistic. The raw sequence itself sits in the same place: CRM's Objectives section says the model documents 'the intellectual structure' of documentation and 'has not been optimised for implementation specific storage and processing factors' -- i.e. it is the wrong home for a specialist payload that a genetic database already curates and versions. So: E17 (+ E15/E42/P70) for the fact and its provenance, no CRM class for the sequence bytes or the tree statistics themselves.

rejected_alternatives.option: Storing the nucleotide sequence itself in the collection database (e.g. as an E90 Symbolic Object/E62 String attached to the specimen)
rejected_alternatives.why_not: duplicates primary data that already lives in the deposited genetic-database record; CRM's Objectives section says the model documents the intellectual structure of documentation, not implementation-specific storage of a specialist dataset, and Issue 76/77's own Natural-History scoping puts only 'ordinary collection management' -- not elaborate derived scientific data -- inside the CRM's practical scope.

rejected_alternatives.option: Modelling the phylogenetic tree's bootstrap-support values as E54 Dimension on the specimen
rejected_alternatives.why_not: E54 Dimension is a quantifiable property of one object determined by one method; a bootstrap-support value is a statistic about an inferred relationship across multiple specimens' sequences, not a property this fish alone has, and CRM/CRMsci has no class for the tree structure it belongs to.

rejected_alternatives.option: E32 Authority Document for the external genetic-database record
rejected_alternatives.why_not: E32 is for encyclopaedias, thesauri and controlled term lists; a single GenBank-style accession entry documenting one specimen's sequence is a record, not an authority list, so plain E31 Document (P70 documents) fits better.
